Application Materials.content:
This section contains information on the required documents you need for your MSc in Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics application, including a personal statement and one academic or professional reference.
| Document | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Personal statement | This should be approximately 500 words in length. |
| Official transcript | If required, please provide a certified English translation. |
| Degree certificate | If required, please provide a certified English translation. This is not required for current students. |
| English language qualification | See Entry Requirements for accepted certificates. |
Please note that we reserve the right to verify documents submitted within your application. A reference is not required as part of your application, however, if you wish to submit a reference in support of your application, you are welcome to. **We reserve the right to request a reference during the application review process. If requested, you will need to submit a suitable reference before we can deliver a result for your application.**
[Admissions documents guidance](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/admissions-documents)
Personal statement: We will be looking for evidence in your personal statement that you have thought carefully about what you can bring to the programme and what impact you feel it will have on your future career. Please ensure that you address the following issues in your statement:
- What skills, qualities and experiences have prepared you to undertake this programme?
- What value do you think you can add to the learning community as part of an internationally diverse group?
- What impact do you hope to make in your future career, and how will this programme contribute to your aspirations?
Your personal statement should be around 500 words in length. The information you give us must be true. Copying information from elsewhere or asking someone else to write your statement, including the use of AI apps such as Chat GPT, could be considered fraud.
For further information regarding references during the application process, visit the University's [references page](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/references).

Academic Requirements.content:
Entrance to the MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme is highly competitive. Applicants can increase their chances of a successful application by exceeding the minimum eligibility criteria through academic grades above standard requirements and/or relevant work experience.
- Applicants need a **UK first-class** or **2:1 honours degree** in one of the following subjects, or an equivalent overseas qualification:
- An undergraduate degree in management science, operational research, statistics, econometrics, mathematics, physics, computer science, or engineering.
- A degree in business, management, finance, or economics that has covered quantitative content.
- Candidates with a very good Honours degree in other areas of study or with relevant work experience will be considered on an individual basis.
- Relevant work experience is not required but may increase chances of acceptance.
- Preference will be given to those with grades above the minimum requirements due to strong competition for places on this programme.
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as their studies will be completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date.
- For overseas students, the minimum academic requirement is a **UK 2:1 honours degree in a related subject** or an **equivalent international qualification**.
- China-specific requirement: **85%+; Band A from the [Priority list of Chinese universities](https://www.ed.ac.uk/sites/default/files/atoms/files/priority_list_of_chinese_universities.pdf)**.
- China-specific requirement from International Qualifications: a **minimum of 85%** awarded by a Chinese university on the Priority List. This degree programme is **Band A**.
- Edinburgh China postgraduate entry guidance for Band A: **a minimum of 85% awarded by a university on the Priority List**.
- The ranking of the university at which applicants studied is considered when determining whether or not a degree is equivalent to a first or upper second-class honours degree in the UK.
- If a degree is not of the required standard and the applicant does not have highly relevant work or other experience, the application will normally be rejected.
- Meeting the degree requirement does not ensure acceptance; a higher standard may be needed for an application to be competitive for admission or funding.
- A conditional offer can be made if an applicant is waiting for a final degree result.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Regardless of your nationality or country of residence, you must demonstrate a level of English language competency which will enable you to succeed in your studies.
English language qualifications accepted at the grades specified:
- [IELTS Academic](https://www.ielts.org/): **total 7.0 with at least 6.0 in each component**. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted to meet English language requirements.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) before 21 January 2026: **total 100 with at least 20 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) from 21 January 2026: **total 5.0 with at least 4.0 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [C1 Advanced](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/) (formerly CAE) / [C2 Proficiency](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/) (formerly CPE): **total 185 with at least 169 in each component**.
- [Trinity ISE](https://www.trinitycollege.com/site/?id=3287): **ISE III with passes in all four components**.
- [Oxford ELLT](https://oxfordellt.com/) (Global and Digital): **8 overall with at least 6 in each component**.
Unless you are a national of a majority English speaking country, your English language qualification must be no more than **three and a half years old** from the start of the month in which the programme begins. If using IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, Trinity ISE, or Oxford ELLT, it must be no more than **two years old** on the first of the month in which the programme begins, regardless of nationality.
Degrees taught and assessed in English are also accepted if the undergraduate or postgraduate degree was taught and assessed in a majority English speaking country, as defined by UK Visas and Immigration: [UKVI list of majority English speaking countries](https://www.gov.uk/tier-4-general-visa/knowledge-of-english). A degree taught and assessed in English from a university on the list of approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries is also accepted: [Approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/entry-requirements/english-requirements/approved-universities). If you are not a national of a majority English speaking country, then your degree must be no more than **five years old** at the start of the month in which your programme begins.
If you already have an English language certificate then you can include this with your application. If you have not yet taken a test, the application will still be processed and you will be able to upload your results when you receive them. A conditional offer may be given if you do not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but you must provide evidence that you have reached the minimum English requirement before an unconditional offer can be provided.
Optional pre-sessional English courses are available. English for Business Masters is for students accepted by the School who have already met the English requirement and want to improve English skills. General English for Academic Purposes is for international students who need to improve their English language level before commencing study; at the end of the course, students undertake an assessment which can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September. [English for Academic Purposes summer courses](https://www.ed.ac.uk/english-language-teaching/pre-sessional-english/summer-eap-courses)

Program Overview.content:
The financial industry is experiencing rapid innovation. From digital banking, it has progressed towards biometric security, the rise of fintech platforms, and the streamlining of banking processes with the use of AI, to name a few. Advancements in the field of analytics are enhancing the ability of banks to predict and manage various kinds of financial risks.
The MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme provides an understanding of the role of banking in the economy, the risk factors, and how to manage these. By meeting the demands of specialist departments within financial firms, this programmes differs from others in the fields of finance or analytics.
- Programme structure: Find an overview of the typical structure of the MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme, including information on compulsory and option courses. [View programme structure](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/programme-structure)
- Learning outcomes: You will gain practical skills in understanding financial statements, predicting risks associated with potential borrowers, and estimating predictive risks using software. [View the learning outcomes](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/learning-outcomes)
- Industry opportunities: Participate in industry treks, group consultancy, client sourced dissertations, and benefit from speaking to a variety of industry professionals. [Engagement with industry](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/industry-opportunities)

Cost of Attendance.content:
For 2026-2027, the University estimates that it will cost an average of **£18,504 each year (£1,542 each month)** to live in Edinburgh as a postgraduate. This amount does not include study costs like tuition fees.
| Living cost item | Per month | Per 52-week year |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| **Accommodation and utilities** | £978 | £11,736 |
| **Food and other shopping** | £248 | £2,976 |
| **Mobile phone contract** | £12 | £144 |
| **Socialising, leisure and wellbeing** | £246 | £2,952 |
| **Local bus travel (age 22+)** | £58 | £696 |
| **Estimated total living costs** | **£1,542** | **£18,504** |
Accommodation and utilities are estimated at **£752 to £1,249 per month**. Postgraduate accommodation options include:
| Cost item | University | Private | Private student |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **Rent for accommodation** | £918 per month (ranging from £388 to £1,596) | £688 per month | £1,227 per month (ranging from £659 to £1,781) |
| **Utilities (gas and electric)** | Included in rent | £55 per month | Included in rent |
| **WiFi** | Included in rent | £9 per month | Included in rent |
| **Laundry services** | £13 per month | Washing machines normally in flats | £22 per month |
| **Estimated total** | **£931 per month** | **£752 per month** | **£1,249 per month** |
Food and other shopping are estimated at **£248 per month**, based on shopping at supermarkets and primarily cooking at home, and including toiletries and cleaning products.
A mobile phone contract is estimated at **£12 per month** for a SIM-only plan.
Socialising, leisure and wellbeing are estimated at **£246 per month** and include costs like sport and society memberships, nights out, eating out, entertainment subscriptions, and gym memberships. Students in Scotland do not need to pay for healthcare or prescriptions, but international students need to pay a health surcharge to access the NHS as part of their visa application.
Local bus travel is estimated at **£58 per month** for students aged 22+, or **£660 for an annual advance purchase pass**. Students under 22 can get free bus travel with the Young Scot National Entitlement Card.

Multiple Applications.content:
#### Do not submit more than five applications
We recommend that you submit only one or two applications in order to have the best possible chance of receiving a positive outcome. We understand that you may find it difficult to choose between one or two related degree programmes, and we are prepared to consider more than one application in those circumstances. However, we cannot consider **more than five applications from the same applicant**, and this number may be lower in high demand areas.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Each year we have limited capacity for deferred offers. All deferral requests will be considered on an individual basis.
- The deadline for submitting a deferral request is **31 August**.
- If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you are encouraged to take up your place for entry this year, or to withdraw and submit a new application for entry next year when applications open. There is no guarantee that a new application will be successful.
- If you defer your place, you may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. The new SELT will be required by **31 October** of your original entry year.
- The deposit must be paid before a deferral is agreed. This should be done within **28 days** of receiving the original offer. The deposit is non-refundable.
- We defer unconditional offers only. It is possible to defer an offer only once.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as your studies will be completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date.
- A conditional offer can be made if you are waiting for a final degree result or a language test result.
- A conditional offer may be given to you if you do not yet meet the minimum English requirement. You must provide evidence that you have reached the minimum English requirement before an unconditional offer can be provided.
- If you require a visa, you must have achieved your English qualification and have met any other conditions to qualify for an unconditional offer, which is a requirement for the CAS. The University will commence issuing CAS from June onwards.
- General English for Academic Purposes is intended for international students who need to improve their English language level prior to commencing a programme of study at the University of Edinburgh. At the end of the course, students undertake an assessment which can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September.
